notes:
RESOLVED — N=128 computes ACROSS TWO DIES, BIT-EXACT: 200 samples into chip 0, 400 words out of chip 1, every one equal to whole(x), 73 non-zero past the latency-127 transient, on the real placed+routed two-chip build through MultiChipSimulation and through the GRC server op. Split after stage 0 (die 0 = 30 cells, the period-64 octant fold; die 1 = 84 cells, stages 1..6, layout hash identical to the verified FFT64).

THE CROSSING WAS INNOCENT — THE FAULT WAS THE DRIVER. A complex sample is a THREE-PART transaction (WRITE xi, WRITE xq, one JUMP) and on the multi-chip path each part must be pumped to quiescence before the next is injected. Measured on the identical bitstream over 12 samples: all-three-queued 0/24 words, two-writes-queued 0/24, WRITE+JUMP-per-word 48/24 (double-fires), PACED 24/24. It hid because both dies were verified through run_block_dut_complex (which paces correctly) while the two-die run used a hand-written driver that did not — the one component that differed between a passing and a failing run was never a suspect. The three earlier inter-chip engine fixes were necessary and correct; they simply were not the last fault.

THREE FURTHER BUGS FOUND AND FIXED: (1) THE BUILD WAS NOT DETERMINISTIC — cpsat_router ran an 8-worker portfolio with no random_seed and its objective has ties, so equal-optimal routings varied between builds (fixed with random_seed + interleave_search; 1211 placekyt tests unregressed); (2) test_kyt_route_transits was CHIP-BLIND, and the gain_2p2s xfail had been documenting that same bug — _KNOWN_OPEN is now empty, 27 gates green, no xfail; (3) route-quality/saturation/orientation coverage gaps the example exposed, each closed with a proof rather than a waiver (notably a WALLED_IN_NETS exception that FLOOD-FILLS to prove die 0's +10 egress really is the shortest path that exists).

SHIPS AS examples/fft128_2die/ — an openable two-chip .kyt, a .grc (0 errors under the real GRC compiler), and a demo whose --pattern batched flag REPRODUCES THE ORIGINAL FAILURE ON DEMAND. 18 gates incl. INV-4 teeth and an unpaced-drive guard. Manifest: the un-instantiable FFT128Block row replaced by FFT128Die0 + FFT128Die1, both done with GRC bindings.
